title: The Bull and the Calf
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A full-grown Bull was struggling to force his huge bulk through the narrow entrance to a cow-house where his stall was, when a young Calf came up and said to him, "If you'll step aside a moment, I'll show you the way to get through." The Bull turned upon him an amused look. "I knew that way," said he, "before you were born."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Bull struggling to do?
options: Break free from a rope tied around his neck
Climb over a low fence into the pasture
Force his huge bulk through the narrow entrance to the cow-house
Push a cart stuck in the mud

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who offers to help the Bull?
options: A young Calf
An older Bull
A farmer nearby
A passing sheep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Calf offer to show the Bull?
options: A different, wider entrance nearby
How to make himself appear smaller
Where the farmer keeps the food
The way to get through the entrance

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Bull react to the Calf's offer?
options: He becomes angry and charges at the Calf
He turns upon him an amused look
He accepts the help gratefully
He ignores the Calf completely

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Bull say he knew before the Calf was born?
options: How to grow to full size
How to behave around farmers
That way, referring to how to get through the entrance
How to find his own stall

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Bull find the Calf's offer amusing rather than helpful?
options: The much younger Calf is offering advice about something the Bull has long since mastered
The Calf's suggestion is factually incorrect about the entrance
The Bull cannot understand what the Calf is trying to say
The Calf is offering to do something physically impossible

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what point does the Bull's reply make about experience and advice?
options: Younger animals are always wrong about practical matters
Calves should never speak to bulls under any circumstances
The entrance was never actually difficult to pass through
Advice can seem out of place when it comes from someone with far less experience than the one receiving it

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "bulk" mean in "his huge bulk"?
options: His strength in a fight
His large size or mass
His speed while running
His stubborn attitude

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Bull gave the Calf "an amused look"?
options: A look showing he was deeply offended
A look showing he was confused by the Calf's words
A look showing he found the offer mildly funny
A look showing he was too tired to respond

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: It can be amusing when the inexperienced try to teach the experienced something they already know well
Young animals should never offer help to older ones
Cow-houses should always have wider entrances
Experience matters less than good intentions when offering help

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where is the Bull trying to go?
options: To the pasture for the night
To a watering hole nearby
To join the other bulls in the field
To his stall in the cow-house

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Calf ask the Bull to do for a moment?
options: Wait quietly
Step aside
Turn around
Lower his head

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the very first word of the Bull's reply to the Calf?
options: "Well"
"No"
"Ha"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why doesn't the Bull actually need the Calf's help to get through the entrance?
options: He has passed through that same entrance many times over the course of his life
The entrance is not actually narrow at all
The Calf's suggested method would not have worked anyway
The Bull has already found another way through by himself

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Bull's calm, amused reaction suggest about how he takes the Calf's offer?
options: He is deeply insulted by such a young animal offering advice
He is worried the Calf might actually know something he doesn't
He is embarrassed to be seen struggling by a Calf
He is not offended, simply finding it lightly funny given his own experience

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "narrow" describe about the entrance?
options: Being unusually tall
Having very little width
Being made of stone
Being newly built

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Calf successfully guides a lost Bull to safety
A Bull refuses ever to enter the cow-house again
A young Calf offers to help a struggling Bull, who points out he has known the way for far longer than the Calf has been alive
A Calf and a Bull argue over who owns the stall
